title: Session status signals
summary: Design and implement session status lanes that distinguish operational action status from informational interpretation signals, including a neutral heat index for hot-work detection and AI-backed session status summaries.

nodes.title: Capture initial shaping
nodes.summary: Preserve the session status brainstorming as a workstream support doc and distill it into the initial brief and graph without making the support doc the current operational source of truth.

nodes.title: Status lane design contract
nodes.summary: Turn the shaping into a project design update that defines operational status versus informational signals, active versus quiet waiting, the neutral heat-index concept, UI hierarchy, runtime status ownership, and boundaries with existing session registry and PAW artifact status.

nodes.title: Status summarizer contract
nodes.summary: Define the structured runtime summary emitted from session state, event history, process/heartbeat state, tracker/PR signals, and AI summary: operational status, waiting recency, reasons, suggested action, informational signals, confidence, and freshness.

nodes.title: Operational status classifier
nodes.summary: Classify sessions into action statuses such as working, needs-builder, quiet-waiting, ready-review, blocked, stale, and closed, with reasons that distinguish fresh conversation-needed from cooled-off conversation-needed, artifact-review-needed, and external-blocker-needed.

nodes.title: Heat index detection
nodes.summary: Compute current, peak, and trend heat signals from builder-agent interaction density, recency, user/assistant alternation, and iteration cues, while making clear that heat is not urgency, quality, or success/failure.

nodes.title: Informational signal surface
nodes.summary: Surface secondary interpretation signals such as needs-reconciliation, boundary pressure, design impact, attachment, environment, and confidence through the session status overlay without making them primary action status.

nodes.title: Session card status lanes
nodes.summary: Update the session card/subcard UI so operational status is visually dominant, quiet-waiting sessions remain findable but lower priority than fresh needs-builder sessions, and informational signals appear as secondary chips or thermal indicators, including an accessible neutral heat dot/ring instead of a fire emoji.

nodes.title: Graph overlay status consumption
nodes.summary: Define the minimal way graph node overlays consume the same session operational-status and informational-signal contract without expanding this workstream into the whole runtime-overlay or portfolio-shell effort.

nodes.title: Real session validation
nodes.summary: Validate the status lanes, heat index, active-vs-quiet waiting, and waiting-vs-review classifier against real cool, warm, hot, blocked, needs-builder, quiet-waiting, and ready-review sessions before promoting the model as the default session status surface.

checkpoints.title: Status model shaped
checkpoints.summary: Initial shaping is preserved and the project design contract for operational status lanes, informational signals, and heat index semantics is accepted.

checkpoints.title: Status detection contract
checkpoints.summary: The summarizer contract, operational classifier, waiting-recency model, heat index, and informational signal model are defined and usable by the session UI.

checkpoints.title: Status UI usable
checkpoints.summary: The Sessions surface separates action status from interpretation signals and graph overlays can consume the same contract without duplicating semantics.

checkpoints.title: Session status signals validated
checkpoints.summary: Real sessions demonstrate that the status model distinguishes needs-builder, quiet-waiting, ready-review, working, blocked, stale, and heat states well enough for the builder to operate from.
